tools.title: Gameplay Tags
tools.summary: Hierarchical identifiers for gameplay state, categories, abilities, effects and cross-system queries.
why: Works with GAS and other systems
workflow: Use tags for semantic state/categories, not arbitrary data.
Validate references and avoid near-duplicate meanings.
tools.codex: Prefer Gameplay Tags when multiple systems need a shared semantic vocabulary.
tools.caution: Tags can become an ungoverned global namespace; maintain conventions.

tools.title: Enhanced Input
tools.summary: Asset-based input actions, triggers, modifiers and mapping contexts for contextual/remappable controls.
workflow: Keep gameplay actions separate from physical keys.
tools.codex: Codex can create consistent input assets/handlers once corresponding MCP asset tools exist.
tools.caution: Avoid binding gameplay logic directly to raw keys throughout Blueprints.

tools.title: Common UI
tools.summary: Layered UI/input framework designed for complex game menus and multi-input navigation.
workflow: Integrate with the current UE 5.8 input model.
Test keyboard/gamepad focus and back/accept behavior.
tools.codex: Useful target architecture for menu-heavy games instead of ad-hoc widget creation/removal.
tools.caution: Adopt for real navigation complexity; simple HUD-only games may not need it.

tools.title: StateTree
tools.summary: Hierarchical state machine combining state-machine transitions with selector-style hierarchy.
workflow: Avoid replacing simple booleans with a StateTree unnecessarily.
tools.codex: Strong candidate for AI/NPC/interactable state systems; we should add dedicated read/write MCP support.
tools.caution: StateTree is an architecture choice, not a universal replacement for Behavior Trees or simple state variables.

tools.title: Gameplay Ability System (GAS)
tools.summary: Framework for abilities, attributes, effects, cues, costs, cooldowns, replication and prediction.
workflow: Put ASC ownership in the correct Actor/PlayerState.
tools.codex: When the game has substantial combat/abilities, prefer GAS over custom one-off cooldown/buff systems.
tools.caution: GAS has a learning/architecture cost; do not add it to a tiny prototype without need.

tools.title: Game Features / Modular Gameplay
tools.summary: Feature-plugin approach for modular gameplay content that can be activated/deactivated independently.
why: Useful for teams working on parallel game features
workflow: Keep a feature's content/code/data inside its feature plugin.
Use shared core modules only for stable contracts.
tools.codex: Good architecture when Codex is tasked with an isolated feature; boundaries make changes safer.
tools.caution: Adds project structure complexity; not required for every small game.

tools.title: Procedural Content Generation (PCG)
tools.summary: Node-based procedural content framework for scattering, generation and data-driven environment workflows.
workflow: Profile generated content and keep runtime/editor generation strategy explicit.
tools.codex: UE 5.8 includes PCG toolsets in the Toolset Registry family, making it a strong target for AI-assisted generation.
tools.caution: Procedural generation can hide performance/content explosion; set budgets and validate outputs.

tools.title: Mass Entity / Mass Framework
tools.summary: Data-oriented entity framework for large numbers of agents/entities and scalable simulation.
workflow: Use only when actor-per-entity architecture becomes a measured bottleneck.
tools.codex: Specialized architecture; Codex should not introduce Mass unless project scale warrants it.
tools.caution: Higher conceptual complexity than Actors/Components; premature adoption can slow development.

tools.title: Blueprint Architecture: Components, Interfaces, Dispatchers & Subsystems
tools.summary: Use composition and explicit contracts to prevent giant, tightly-coupled Blueprint classes.
workflow: Put reusable actor behavior in Actor Components.
Use Blueprint Interfaces for capability contracts.
Use Event Dispatchers for one-to-many notifications.
Keep widgets as presentation, not game-state owners.
tools.codex: Default architecture rules for generated Blueprint systems; refactor before graphs become giant.
tools.caution: Do not replace every direct reference with an interface/event; choose the simplest decoupling that fits ownership.

tools.title: C++ / Blueprint Boundary Strategy
tools.summary: Keep stable/high-performance/framework code in C++ and fast content/gameplay iteration in Blueprints.
workflow: Keep tuning/content assembly in Blueprint/Data Assets.
Move hotspots or fragile duplicated logic to C++ only when justified.
tools.codex: Codex should choose the lane deliberately instead of converting everything to C++ or leaving everything in Blueprint.
tools.caution: Avoid blueprint-only private engine reimplementations and avoid C++ for every tiny designer-tuned behavior.

tools.title: Naming & Folder Conventions
tools.summary: Consistent asset prefixes, feature folders and ownership boundaries make large Unreal projects searchable and automatable.
why: Codex can infer asset intent from names
workflow: Define prefixes for major asset types.
Avoid dumping assets into generic Misc folders.
tools.codex: Naming conventions directly improve agent search precision and reduce accidental edits.
tools.caution: Do not over-engineer names with excessive abbreviations; optimize for team comprehension and automation.

tools.title: Lyra Sample Game as Architecture Reference
tools.summary: Epic-maintained modular multiplayer sample demonstrating modern UE architecture including Game Features, GAS, Enhanced Input and scalable UI/gameplay patterns.
why: Real production-style examples instead of isolated snippets
Strong reference for multiplayer, abilities, inventory/equipment and UI architecture
workflow: Install the Lyra version matching the target engine.
Study one subsystem relevant to the current feature instead of copying the whole project.
Document the pattern and why it fits your game.
Implement a smaller project-specific version and validate complexity before expanding.
tools.codex: Codex can use Lyra as a pattern reference, but should not cargo-cult class names or architecture that the current game does not need.
tools.caution: Lyra is a learning/reference project, not a mandatory starter architecture; its complexity can be excessive for small games.
